skill.name: one-pass
skill.description: Reduce repeated work with acceptance checks, focused source reading, batched actions, bounded retries, and complete delegation briefs.
skill.summary: Plan, verify, and hand off deliverables with fewer repeated steps while preserving safety checks.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives involving Markdown examples, verification guidance, or delegation checklist text. No evidence found of malicious execution, reconnaissance, exfiltration, or instructions to bypass security analysis in the two reviewed files.

finding_verdicts.reason: The checklist asks delegation briefs to list past rejections and banned items. This records task constraints, not host discovery or system reconnaissance.
Backticks format the example pipe to head in Markdown, rather than executable Ruby or shell substitution. The surrounding text recommends filtering large outputs locally.
Backticks enclose the relative documentation path references/checklists.md. The instruction requests acceptance checks and reading a reference section, not command execution.
Backticks enclose a sample status receipt reporting passes, rereads, and retries. This is output formatting, with no executable payload or command substitution.
The text explicitly prohibits using force flags, --no-verify, or destructive shortcuts to save tokens. Backticks mark a prohibited flag, not an execution instruction.
The sentence requires honest disclosure of unverified work. It contains no request to enumerate the host, inspect credentials, or gather system information.

content.value_statement: Repeated reading, unclear requirements, and blind retries waste tokens and delay delivery. One Pass structures acceptance checks, focused evidence gathering, verification, and delegation to reduce avoidable rework.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of a short acceptance list from user requirements, project rules, and previous feedback.
Recommends targeted source reads and a factual ledger to reduce repeated reading.
Organizes independent actions into batches and limits repeated unsuccessful approaches.
Provides verification checklists for code, visuals, video, copy, data changes, reports, and delegation briefs.
Structures complete handoff briefs with exact inputs, acceptance checks, exclusions, and reporting requirements.
Requires safety approvals, secret protection, and disclosure of unverified results throughout the workflow.
limitations: Provides written workflow guidance, not an executable automation engine or enforced token budget.
Cannot guarantee first-pass correctness or a specific reduction in token usage.
Requires task-specific tools and access to perform tests, inspect media, or verify system changes.
Retry limits and focused reading must not replace required reviews, permissions, or verification.

use_cases.title: Verify a focused code change
use_cases.description: Define acceptance checks, inspect relevant sources, make the requested change, and run focused tests before reporting completion.

use_cases.title: Review a campaign deliverable
use_cases.description: Check copy, dimensions, factual claims, brand requirements, and visual readability against an explicit brief.

use_cases.title: Prepare a complete agent handoff
use_cases.description: Combine exact inputs, constraints, acceptance criteria, and evidence requirements into a single delegation brief.

prompt_templates.title: Review a simple deliverable
prompt_templates.prompt: Use One Pass to review [deliverable] against [requirements]. Identify unmet checks and clearly state anything you cannot verify.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review an existing result against a short brief.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a focused change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use One Pass for [task] in [project]. Define acceptance checks, inspect relevant sources, complete the work, and report verification evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: deliver a bounded task with focused validation.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose repeated failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use One Pass to resolve [failure]. Review [error evidence] and [previous attempts]. Test one hypothesis, change approach when needed, and report blockers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: stop blind retries and investigate a recurring failure.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate independent subtasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use One Pass to coordinate [project]. Separate independent subtasks, write complete briefs, define shared acceptance checks, and require evidence before integration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: organize delegated work with explicit verification and handoffs.

output_examples.input: Review a promotional banner against the supplied brief.
output: Acceptance checks: required dimensions, exact offer, correct contact details, and readable text.
Verified: dimensions and contact details match the brief.
Correction required: the offer date differs from the source.
Not checked: appearance after publication on the target platform.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff for an agent updating an approved settings field.
output: Goal: update only the approved notification setting.
Inputs: the supplied record identifier and approved value.
Constraints: preserve unrelated fields and request approval before any destructive action.
Acceptance: read the changed field back from the system and confirm the approved value.
Report: identify the updated record, provide verification evidence, and list any blockers.

best_practices: Provide exact requirements, authoritative sources, and previous rejection reasons before work begins.
Choose verification evidence that directly demonstrates each acceptance criterion.
Keep secrets out of notes and briefs, and preserve all required permissions and safety reviews.
anti_patterns: Treating a successful edit operation as proof that the resulting behavior is correct.
Repeating failed commands without testing a new hypothesis or changing the approach.
Delegating vague tasks without exact inputs, constraints, or evidence requirements.

faq.question: Does One Pass guarantee success on the first attempt?
faq.answer: No. It reduces avoidable rework through clearer requirements and verification, but cannot guarantee correctness.

faq.question: Does it enforce a token budget?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance for reducing repeated work, not usage metering or hard token limits.

faq.question: Which deliverables have checklists?
faq.answer: The reference covers code, images, posts, banners, slides, video, copy, data, settings, records, reports, analyses, and delegation briefs.

faq.question: Does it replace task-specific skills?
faq.answer: No. It organizes the workflow around task-specific skills, project rules, and available tools.

faq.question: How does it handle repeated failures?
faq.answer: After two failures with the same approach, it calls for diagnosis and a changed approach instead of another blind retry.

faq.question: Can it skip safety checks to save tokens?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly preserves confirmations, reviews, tests, secret protection, and approval before installing or running new tools for token savings.
